data.name: Dharaani
data.gender_notes: Dharaani is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Hindu mythology, Dharaani represents the divine power that supports and nourishes all creation. The name signifies strength, resilience, and the ability to carry the weight of the universe. The name Dharaani carries the meaning “One who carries, supports” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Dharaani usually hope their child will grow to embody one who carries, supports and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the divine power that carries and sustains the universe.
data.etymology: Dharaani belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “One who carries, supports.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Dharaani total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Dharaani" holds deep cultural significance in Hinduism. It is believed that the divine goddesses Dhara (the one who holds or supports) and Dharani (the earth or the ground) are embodiments of this essential force. Dharaani is often invoked in various religious rituals for strength, protection, and blessings.
data.spiritual_significance: Spiritually, Dharaani represents the root or foundation that sustains life at all levels - physical, mental, and spiritual. It reflects the concept of unwavering faith and unyielding support. The name inspires confidence, courage, and resilience amidst life's trials and tribulations, encouraging the belief that even in chaos and turmoil, one can remain firm, grounded, and steadfast.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The name Dharaani signifies the ever-flowing river of life, carrying the essence of creation and nourishing all beings with its divine nectar. It is a reminder of the eternal and unchanging nature of the universe, nurturing and supporting us through life's challenges.

vedic_reference.note: The name Dharaani is derived from the Sanskrit word Dhara, meaning 'earth', and Ani, meaning 'residence'. It is a beautiful and meaningful name for a baby girl, evoking a sense of connection to the earth and a sense of stability and nurturing.

historical_references.reference:
Dharaani was a queen of the Satavahana Dynasty, ruling in the 2nd century AD. She is known for her patronage of Buddhism and her role in the expansion of Buddhist influence in the Deccan region.
Reference: Mitra, S. (2002). Ancient Indian History and Civilization. New Age International (India) Ltd. 
Context: Political and Religious History of India.

Dharaani was also the name of a goddess revered in ancient Hinduism, particularly in the southern Indian states of Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh. She is believed to have the power to protect her devotees from evil and bring prosperity.
Reference: Subrahmanyam, K. (1996). A Historical Dictionary of Ancient India. ABC-CLIO.
Context: Hindu Religion and Mythology.
